Chapter 4: The Habits and Behaviors That Build Lasting Confidence
When you think about confidence, it’s easy to picture it as something you either have or you don’t.
But here’s the thing—confidence isn’t fixed. It’s actually built up, little by little, through the habits and behaviors you practice every day. Some folks might seem naturally self-assured, but truly, anyone can strengthen their confidence with the right tools and mindsets.
One of the most powerful ways to grow your confidence? Take action. Every time you step out of your comfort zone—even if it’s just a tiny step—you give yourself proof that you’re capable. Maybe it’s speaking up in a meeting, learning a new skill, or just going after a goal that feels a little daunting.
Each of these actions sends a message to yourself: “Hey, I can do this. I’m resilient.”
Picture this process as a kind of spiral. When you take action, you gain experience. That experience builds your competence, and the more competent you feel, the more confident you become.
The more you repeat this cycle, the stronger your self-assurance gets.
So what habits actually help this confidence spiral? Here are a few to keep in mind:
First, take initiative. Step up for new projects, share your ideas, or look for challenges—even when you feel a bit unsure.
Next, embrace imperfection. Let go of the idea that you have to be flawless. Mistakes aren’t just normal—they’re part of learning and growing.
Practice self-reflection. Take time to notice your strengths and areas where you want to grow. And do it with kindness toward yourself.
Seek feedback. Ask others for their input, but don’t let it define your worth. Use it as a way to improve and move forward.
And celebrate small wins. Every achievement matters, no matter how minor it seems. Let those little victories fuel your momentum.
Now, let’s talk about something almost everyone struggles with: negative self-talk. That inner critic loves to amplify doubts and ignore your successes, especially for women.
But you can actually challenge those thoughts and swap them out for something more supportive. For example, instead of saying, “I’m not ready for this,” try, “I might not know everything yet, but I can learn as I go.”
That simple shift in perspective can take the edge off anxiety and make it easier to take action.
Building confidence also means learning to handle fear of failure. Confident people don’t avoid risks—they see setbacks as chances to grow. They ask themselves, “What can I learn from this?” and “How can I use it next time?”
But you don’t have to do this alone. Supportive relationships really matter here. Having mentors, thoughtful peers, or allies gives you someone to lean on, share struggles with, and get real advice. Being part of a community that encourages growth and resilience makes it so much easier to take risks—and bounce back when things don’t go as planned.
And let’s not forget about workplace culture. A place that rewards risk-taking, accepts mistakes, and celebrates different perspectives? That’s the kind of environment where confidence can really grow. On the flip side, if mistakes are punished or there’s pressure to just fit in, it can really hold people back.
So, what can you do, practically, to boost your confidence every day?
Try setting stretch goals—choose something just challenging enough, and break it down into steps you can manage.
Practice assertive communication. Speak up for your needs, share your opinions, and set boundaries clearly and respectfully.
Make a growth plan. Pinpoint where you want to develop, and look for resources, training, or experiences that can help you get there.
And finally, take a moment now and then to reflect on your progress. Maybe keep a journal of your achievements, challenges, and what you’ve learned along the way.
By weaving these habits into your daily life, confidence becomes part of who you are.
Over time, those small actions add up—giving you a rock-solid foundation of self-assurance that can support you in every part of your life.
